language_wrapper: In a round‐robin tournament with {team_count} teams labeled 1 through {team_count}, each unordered pair of distinct teams plays exactly {rounds_per_pair} independent games. Team i has a positive strength s_i, and the ordered list of strengths is {strengths} (so s_1, s_2, …, s_{team_count} are given in that order). In any single game between teams i and j, the probability that i wins is s_i/(s_i + s_j); there are no ties, and all games are mutually independent. Let the probability that the tournament produces neither a team that wins all its games nor a team that loses all its games be equal to m/d in lowest terms. Find m + d.
hardness_rationale: The seed problem relies on symmetry with equal win probabilities and a single game per pair, making the inclusion–exclusion computation short. This family introduces Bradley–Terry weights s_i and multiple games per pair, destroying symmetry and forcing careful weighted counting. The inclusion–exclusion still truncates at pair intersections, but evaluating terms requires products of rational probabilities over many edges and exponents r, and ensuring i undefeated/j winless intersections are handled without double-counting the shared games. The larger team counts (n ≥ 6) and r ≥ 2 increase algebraic and combinatorial complexity beyond the seed.
notes: Proof outline: Define events U_i (team i wins all its games) and L_i (team i loses all its games). In a round-robin with any probabilities and independent games, two U_i events cannot both occur because teams i and j play each other; similarly, two L_i events cannot both occur; and U_i ∩ L_i is impossible. Therefore, by inclusion–exclusion, P(no U_i and no L_i) = 1 − ∑_i P(U_i) − ∑_i P(L_i) + ∑_{i≠j} P(U_i ∩ L_j). Independence implies: P(U_i) = ∏_{k≠i} (s_i/(s_i + s_k))^{r}, P(L_i) = ∏_{k≠i} (s_k/(s_i + s_k))^{r}. For intersections with i ≠ j, all r games between i and j must be i wins, all r games between i and k (k ≠ i, j) must be i wins, and all r games between j and k (k ≠ i, j) must be k wins; thus P(U_i ∩ L_j) = (s_i/(s_i + s_j))^{r} × ∏_{k≠i,j} (s_i/(s_i + s_k))^{r} × ∏_{k≠i,j} (s_k/(s_k + s_j))^{r}. All higher-order intersections among these extremes are null, so inclusion–exclusion truncates. The verifier computes the exact rational value via Fractions, ensuring correctness. Difficulty safeguards: n ≥ 6, r ≥ 2, and at least three distinct strengths prevent reduction to the symmetric single-round seed.
source_question: In a five-team tournament, each team plays one game with every other team. Each team has a $50\%$ chance of winning any game it plays. (There are no ties.) Let $\dfrac{m}{n}$ be the probability that the tournament will produce neither an undefeated team nor a winless team, where $m$ and $n$ are relatively prime integers. Find $m+n$ .
